AzureBlobStorage._COMMENT: DEMO ONLY -- REPLACE ConnectionString WITH YOUR REAL AZURE STORAGE CONNECTION STRING. Azure Portal -> scoramstorage -> Security + networking -> Access keys -> Key 1 -> Connection string. Never commit the real value -- see appsettings.Production.json (gitignored) or environment variables instead.

Msg91._COMMENT: DEMO ONLY -- REPLACE AuthKey WITH YOUR REAL MSG91 AUTH KEY (MSG91 dashboard -> Authkey, NOT either widget's own tokenAuth -- see Msg91Service's own comment on the difference). Never commit real values -- see appsettings.Production.json (gitignored) or Render environment variables instead. MSG91 restricts one widget to ONE integration type (Web OR Mobile), so this app runs two separate OTP widgets on the same MSG91 account: Web*** is read by GET /api/auth/otp-widget-config?platform=web, Mobile*** by ?platform=mobile. Each WidgetId/TokenAuth pair is that widget's own client-facing credential (MSG91 dashboard -> OTP -> Widget) -- not a server secret, so it's fine to hand out to whichever client asks (ScoramWeb's own Web pair is embedded directly via a Vite env var instead, bypassing this endpoint entirely -- see ScoramWeb/src/lib/msg91.js and .env.example).

Firebase._COMMENT: DEMO ONLY -- mobile push (FCM). ServiceAccountKeyPath is a path on THIS SERVER to the service-account JSON you download from Firebase Console -> Project settings -> Service accounts -> Generate new private key. Leave blank to leave mobile push disabled (see Services/PushNotificationService.cs -- same no-op-until-configured pattern as VapidKeys/Msg91). Never commit the real JSON file -- keep it outside the repo (or gitignored) same as the Azure connection string above.

Captcha._COMMENT: Signing secret for the app's own lightweight math captcha (see Services/CaptchaService.cs) -- NOT a third-party key, generate any long random string yourself (e.g. `openssl rand -base64 32`) and keep it out of source control same as Jwt:Key. Falls back to Jwt:Key if left blank so a fresh clone still works out of the box, but a dedicated secret here is safer for production so a captcha-token leak/replay can't be combined with anything JWT-related.
